decisions.label: Overlap I/O
decisions.brief: Off: the experts are computed on the device, beside its cache.
decisions.reason: overlap hides the CPU's expert compute behind the streamer's reads, and with the device expert cache armed the experts are computed on CUDA1, so there is nothing on the CPU for it to hide

decisions.label: Device expert cache
decisions.brief: A 34.1 GiB cache of the most used experts on CUDA1, in place of whole layers' experts.
decisions.reason: the experts used most live on the processor that computes them fastest, as the RAM cache holds what flash would read: CUDA1 computes this model's experts at 633 GiB/s against the host's 213, both measured on this model's own expert block; a cache of 34935 MiB (34874 the capacity fitter gave 27 of 45 layers' experts, 60 it left free under one more whole layer) serves 60% of a token's routed bytes (the fraction of the expert set it holds); measured: 16.10 tok/s with a device cache against 14.05 with the fitter's p; a miss is uploaded from the host

decisions.label: Batch width
decisions.brief: This load times the graph 4096 tokens wide, against its own width timed before.
decisions.reason: the devices' compute buffers at the full width are past their share of the cards' memory, which a narrower graph gives the experts; the full width was timed at 16 tok/s, and this load times 4096 tokens

decisions.label: Layer placement
decisions.brief: 47 layers on a device; 45 of 45 layers keep their experts on the CPU.
decisions.reason: the capacity fitter found a placement that is projected to fit; 45 of 45 MoE layers keep their experts on the host, host-resident 418 MiB, on devices 10398 MiB, context 16384 (fitter's host breakdown: model 22571, context 34, compute 384 MiB; file 62542, experts 58124)

decisions.label: Context
decisions.brief: 16384 tokens of context, as given: not weighed against the cache.
decisions.reason: the value this run was given, not a choice: the capacity fitter only picks a context when it is handed a zero and this planner always pins it, so nothing has weighed this number against what the memory it reserves would buy as expert cache

decisions.label: Streaming mode
decisions.brief: The whole model (57.2 GiB) fits in the 192.9 GiB usable.
decisions.reason: on the host 58570 MiB (dense 446) against 197557 MiB usable, which is the 246947 MiB this process may hold (as reported available, unmeasured) less a 49389 MiB margin (the process is killed)

decisions.label: Experts in a device's host memory
decisions.brief: The experts copied into CUDA1's own host memory, for the cache's misses.
decisions.reason: a miss reaches CUDA1 at 10.8 GiB/s from the file's mapping and at 22.5 from the backend's own host memory; the copy takes 58124 MiB, inside the 197557 MiB the host may hold with the 58570 MiB it already does

decisions.label: Expert streaming
decisions.brief: Not streamed: the whole model fits in memory.
decisions.reason: the host residual fits: llama.cpp's placement is the whole plan

decisions.label: Compute threads
decisions.brief: 32 threads: measured on this model, the fastest decode against 23 and 47.
decisions.reason: measured on this model: an earlier load's first answer decoded in alternating windows with 32, 23 and 47 threads, 2 rounds each between two of the incumbent's; the best other count was -0%, inside the 10% margin, so 32 held
